newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen pushing higher on S&P news.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen pushing higher on S&P news.

text.p: Argentine stocks were expected to resume their upward bounce at the opening Wednesday on follow-through momentum from Tuesday's good credit rating news, dealers said.

"The market has totally changed its mood thanks to Standard & Poor's upgrades for several banks and corporate debt issuers," one trader said. "This turn of events could mean institutional cash flows finally rise and allow the bolsa to resume the upward trend that stalled in March.
S&P Tuesday raised the foreign debt counterparty ratings of three banking institutions to BBB-, or investment grade.

In connection with its revised policy affecting issuers in dollarized economies, S&P also raised its ratings on foreign currency debt issued by several leading companies to BBB-, higher than the sovereign debt rating of BB.
"Argentina has received a huge boost and investors will be adjusting their portfolios accordingly," another trader said.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV rose 2.4 percent to 714.77 Tuesday, halting a three-session slide.
"The market will attempt to pierce its first technical resistance level at 720 today and aim for the second target of 740 in the near-term," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.
"The market will remain wary of the volatile trend on Wall Street, but it's been boosted by CS First Boston's portfolio changes," Bonanno said.
The U.S. investment bank Tuesday raised Argentine positions to overweight from neutral in its Latin American model portfolio.
